newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi jobless rate drops to 4.5 pct in Dec..
newsitem.headline: Mississippi jobless rate drops to 4.5 pct in Dec..

text.p: Mississippi's unemployment rate edged down to 4.5 percent in December from 4.8 percent in November and 5.2 percent a year ago, the state Employment Security Commission said Friday.
The December rate was the lowest for that month since 1973.
For the year, Mississippi's unemployment rate averaged 5.9 percent, the lowest annual average since 1979, said Raiford Crews, the commission's chief of labor market information.
"This is truly an outstanding record for Mississippi's economy because for three consecutive years, the state's unemploymenbt rate has been less than 7 percent."

Total nonfarm employment was 1.07 million for December, an increase of 1,800 jobs over the year. Goods-producing jobs declined by 10,200 jobs but that was more than offset by a gain of 12,100 jobs in services.
The largest losses were in transportation equipment manufacturing, food, textiles and apparel, while trade, health services, amusements and government saw the biggest job gains.

"We expect more job gains as we move inot 1997 since the economy has weathered most of the industry downsizing," Crews said. "Growth is expected in trade and services as firms make adjustments brought on by the increased minimum wage."
Crews said manufacturing was expected to regain some of its losses, but services will account for most of the job growth in the coming year.
Lafayette County had the state's lowest unemployment rate for December, 1.5 percent, while Sharkey County had the highest, 19 percent.
Crews said that generally, agricultural areas had the highest unemployment rates and that joblessness in those regions may rise further in January due to seasonal factors and inclement weather.
